In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the following questions: How to partition and repartition large graphs on modern parallel architectures?
the following questions: How to design efficient graph partitioners and repartitioners for modern parallel architectures?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance impact of the non uniform network communication cost and contention on the memory system is not always significant, and the performance impact of these factors is workload dependent.
, for a given graph workload, the performance of the workload is not necessarily proportional to the amount of data communication.

the performance impact of contention on shared resources in memory subsystems can be the dominant factor limiting the scalability of a workload, and that the runtime characteristics of a workload can be used to improve its scalability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to design scalable graph (repartitioners), one needs to understand and take into account the performance impact of the following factors: (1) network communication costs, (2) contention for the memory subsystems of modern multicore machines, and (3) runtime characteristics of the graph workload.
we found that the performance impact of the network communication costs can be significant for large scale graph computation.
we have proposed and implemented a new architecture aware graph repartitioner and workload aware graph partitioner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can achieve better scalability of distributed graph computation by (1) balancing the data communication cost across the entire network; (2) balancing the data contention across all the memory subsystems; and (3) minimizing the runtime overhead of the (re)partitioning process.
, in addition to the network communication, contention on the shared hardware resources in the memory subsystems is also a critical bottleneck of distributed graph processing.

the memory subsystem contention is the main factor in limiting the performance of distributed graph computation on modern multicore clusters, and that it is necessary for graph (re)partitio- ners to consider the workload runtime characteristics in order to achieve good performance.
